title: TensorCore concat OOM + driver/library mismatch — repro journal
content:
Quick scratchpad for a reproducible-ish sequence that hits an OOM during a big concat op that only appears when driver/library mix is off. Purpose: capture commands run, observed outputs, and a short hypothesis tree so I can hand to SRE or continue tomorrow. Notes are messy — this is a scratchpad, not a playbook.

TL;DR: On node a100-40gb-03 (A100 40GB, MIG disabled) running a container built from conda env (torch 2.2.0+cu118 wheel) we see intermittent CUDA OOM inside a concat of sharded tensors. Symptoms correlate with a userspace libtorch linked against a slightly newer libcudart / libcuda ABI while host driver is NVIDIA 525.89.01 (noted mismatch warnings). When LD_PRELOADing a local libcuda shim the OOM goes away but causes occasional device reset traces in dmesg.

Hardware / environment snapshot:
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (PCIe? it is SXM4 on this node)
- Host driver (nvidia-smi): 525.89.01
- CUDA toolkit present in container: /opt/cuda-11.8
- Python env: conda (env name: runtime-debug-2026), python 3.10, pytorch 2.2.0+cu118 wheel built from our CI (libtorch bundled)
- Container runtime: docker 24.0, runc 1.1.9

Commands run (order matters):
1) nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY --format=csv
Output snippet: 
name, memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB], memory.free [MiB]
A100-SXM4-40GB, 40960 MiB, 6144 MiB, 34816 MiB
(looking healthy initially)

2) python -c 'import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))'
Output: 
2.2.0+cu118
11.8
_CudaDeviceProperties(name='A100-SXM4-40GB', major=8, minor=0, total_memory=40960MB, multi_processor_count=108)

3) reproduced failing job (mini reproducer):
- create three large tensors and torch.cat along dim=1 inside half precision pipeline
- small script attached at bottom (repro_cat.py)
Observed stack trace when it fails: 
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro_cat.py", line 58, in <module>
    out = torch.cat(shards, dim=1)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 9.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 6.00 GiB already allocated; 9.00 GiB free; 34.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

But note: sometimes the job succeeds (same inputs) — non-deterministic.

4) dmesg immediately after an OOM: 
[  142.213456] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:3B:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  142.213462] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3B:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
(also a few lines later)
[  142.214000] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x24:0xffff:0x20)

5) ldd check inside container on libtorch: 
$ ldd /opt/conda/envs/runtime-debug-2026/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so 
 -> shows libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so (shim from container image)

6) Checked host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 version: 
- host has /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 symlink to libcuda.so.525.89.01
- container image earlier in CI included /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so which is the CUDA toolkit stub (zero-op) and can mask a proper driver.

7) Attempted quick mitigation: remove stubs from image (mount host /usr/lib into container) -> the stack trace changes: now runtime prints a driver/runtime version mismatch: 
"CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version"
which also causes process to exit earlier instead of OOM.

8) More experiments: LD_PRELOAD=/host/overrides/libcuda.so.1 (a shim that forwards to host driver)
- With this preload, the concat usually succeeds, but dmesg shows periodic NVGPC faults and a single device reset later. Behavior: fewer OOMs, occasional recoverable device resets.

9) git-bisect style check: swapped in earlier torch wheel (2.1.0+cu117) -> fewer OOMs but still occasional; suggests multiple factors (runtime/binary differences matter).

Key error snippets captured in logs:
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 9.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 6.00 GiB already allocated; 9.00 GiB free; 34.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"
- "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" and Xid=79 entries in kernel logs
- "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" (when stubs are present)
- ld.so warnings about symbol versions: "version `GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found" showing up in unrelated times (note: probably from another wheel in image)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Library shadowing: The container image contains CUDA stubs or mismatched libcuda which causes subtle differences; sometimes the stub path is used, resulting in weird reserved memory bookkeeping by the runtime -> OOMs. Evidence: removing stubs changes behavior to clearer driver mismatch.
2) Driver/runtime ABI mismatch: Host driver (525.x) and cu118 runtime/libtorch expect slightly different API semantics — this can cause memory accounting errors or kernel failures, leading to device reset (dmesg) and OOM symptoms. Evidence: different torch wheels change failure frequency.
3) Device-side memory fragmentation / tensor allocation ordering sensitivity: The concat creates a temporary large allocation pattern that interacts poorly with the allocator if earlier fragmentation exists. Non-determinism fits fragmentation. But fragmentation alone doesn't explain the driver reset/Xid=79.
4) Kernel or microcode bug in driver 525.89.01 with specific tensor shapes causing NVLink/TPC path to crash. Evidence: NVGPC/NVGPU messages in dmesg with device reset.
5) Accidental mixed usage of MIG slices vs full device -> different visible memory. (But MIG is disabled on affected node.)

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Rebuild a minimal container without CUDA stubs (remove /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs) and ensure libcuda comes from host (mount host libcuda path). Try reproducer 50x.
- Run reproducer under nsight or cuda-memcheck (expensive) to see if a device-side error appears before OOM. Command: "cuda-memcheck python repro_cat.py" (note: cuda-memcheck might hide device resets).
- Instrument torch allocations: set TORCH_USE_RTLD_GLOBAL? and TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6 to see if reducing reserved behavior changes repro probability. Also try torch.cuda.mem_get_info() before and after big ops to track fragmentation.
- Try a different driver (tested briefly on 530.xx in staging — fewer problems) -> need SRE approval to change driver on prod node.
- Capture full ldd of all C-extension shared objects in the env to look for other lib shadowing (nccl, libcusparse, etc).

Notes to self / random breadcrumbs:
- I saw a stack where libnccl.so was picking up a local copy in /opt/nccl/lib that was built against CUDA 12 dev headers — that seems bad. Add to checklist.
- The LD_PRELOAD shim I used is dumb: it re-exports symbols but loses some private entrypoints; it's only a debugging aid. Don't promote as a fix.
- Reproducer script uses torch.cat on [B, S, d] halves into Bx(3S)xD which allocates 3x memory momentarily. If memory pooling/reservation behavior differs by libtorch build then same logical request may overflow.

Questions for SRE / runtime team:
- Are there any known regressions in 525.89.01 with A100 SXM4 and cu11.8? (I couldn't find release note items matching Xid=79 pattern but release notes are large.)
- Can we get a variant node with 530.x driver to test at scale?
- Do we have a canonical minimal container practice (we shouldn't ship CUDA stubs in image)? Where is the CI check that prevents shipping stubs?

Minimal repro (repro_cat.py) — quick copy: 
import torch
B, S, D = 2, 10240, 512
shards = [torch.empty((B, S, D), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16) for _ in range(3)]
# prefill to create fragmentation
pad = torch.empty((B, 16, D), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16)
for i in range(10):
    t = torch.empty((B, 512, D), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16)
    del t
torch.cuda.synchronize()
# now the cat that sometimes OOMs
out = torch.cat(shards, dim=1)
print('done', out.shape)

If handing off: include the container image tag: registry.redwood-inference/internal/runtime:2026-02-debug-1 (contains the stubs). Also include the host node: a100-40gb-03 (ip x.x.x.x), kernel 6.1.0-35-generic.

Leave this here as a running log. Will try mount-based test tomorrow and run 100 iterations with and without LD_PRELOAD shim and record the pass/fail counts. Also want to ask build team whether our PyTorch wheel is being linked with rpath entries that prefer bundled stubs.

End of scratch.
